quote: **[Surviving Schizophrenia for Families](https://www.amazon.com/dp/1593852738)** — Kim Mueser & Susan Gingerich.
problem: Title/author conflation: "Surviving Schizophrenia" is E. Fuller Torrey's family manual, while the linked ISBN (978-1593852733, Guilford) and the annotation ("Updated comprehensive family guide... from leading researchers") match Mueser & Gingerich's "The Complete Family Guide to Schizophrenia." A student who recommends "Surviving Schizophrenia by Mueser and Gingerich" to a family sends them hunting for a book that does not exist under that pairing, or lands them on Torrey's differently-authored book, and repeats a false attribution on rounds.
replacement: **[The Complete Family Guide to Schizophrenia](https://www.amazon.com/dp/1593852738)** — Kim Mueser & Susan Gingerich.
basis: Publisher records: Guilford ISBN 978-1593852733 is Mueser & Gingerich, The Complete Family Guide to Schizophrenia (2006); "Surviving Schizophrenia: A Family Manual" is Torrey (Harper). Checking the linked product page against the printed title would settle it.

quote: SSRIs/SNRIs plus exposure-based therapy are first-line across anxiety, OCD, and PTSD — standing benzodiazepines are a trap on the unit.
problem: Read distributively — the way a shelf-prepping MS3 will read a can't-miss-style summary line — this licenses "an SNRI is first-line for OCD," which no major guideline supports: first-line OCD pharmacotherapy is an SSRI (clomipramine next), and the same catalog's own OCD string says "exposure and response prevention plus a higher-dose SSRI." SNRIs (venlafaxine, duloxetine) are first-line for GAD, panic, social anxiety, and PTSD only; on the shelf, choosing an SNRI as first-line for OCD is a wrong answer this sentence would have taught.
replacement: SSRIs plus exposure-based therapy are first-line across anxiety, OCD, and PTSD (SNRIs are first-line alternatives for the anxiety disorders and PTSD, not OCD) — standing benzodiazepines are a trap on the unit.
basis: APA practice guideline for OCD (SSRIs first-line, clomipramine second; venlafaxine less well studied) and NICE CG31 (SSRI or clomipramine); venlafaxine is first-line for PTSD in VA/DoD and APA PTSD guidance and for GAD/panic/social anxiety in APA/NICE guidance. Internal consistency: the adjacent string "OCD: exposure and response prevention plus a higher-dose SSRI."
